"The news article discusses the search for an Indian tourist, Vijaya Lakshmi Gali, who disappeared into a sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The sinkhole, which was 8 meters deep, opened up beneath her as she was walking along a road on August 23rd. Rescue efforts have stalled, as the authorities have deemed the operation too risky, citing the safety and health of the rescue personnel. The search has involved various techniques, including tracker dogs, remote cameras, and ground-penetrating radar, but no trace of the victim has been found except for her slippers.

* The authorities have flushed portions of the underground drainage system using high-pressure water jets and excavators to remove debris, but two divers who entered the sinkhole were quickly pulled out due to the dangerous conditions. The article also mentions that a soil slip was reported in the same location the previous year, suggesting the area may be prone to such incidents.

The search for Vijaya Lakshmi Gali has been ongoing for eight days, but the authorities have now decided to halt the operation, deeming it too risky to continue. The incident highlights the dangers of sinkholes and the challenges faced by rescue teams in such situations.
